question: Does the shallow-soil wetness association with strong chorus activation persist when the matched comparison is not wholly confined to the NAAMP 0-3-day post-rain target window?
sample: Weather-qualified pairs constructed exactly by run_naamp_soil_moisture_cue.py.
primary_subset: dry_days_since_rain >= 4. Because the wet member has smaller DaysSinceRain, this excludes comparisons where both surveys lie within 0-3 days after rain.
secondary_subset: wet_days_since_rain >= 4, placing both surveys outside the 0-3-day window.
model: strong_new_score ~ rain_contrast + rain72_amount_difference_z + soil1_gain_difference_z + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber), route-clustered covariance.
secondary_gate: >=150 pairs and >=100 routes; directional diagnostic only, no formal pass gate.
same_observer_primary: Repeat primary subset in same-observer + physically stable pairs if >=1000 pairs and >=250 routes.
interpretation: A primary pass constrains simple 0-3-day protocol targeting as a sufficient explanation for the soil-water association.
It does not eliminate all scheduling or time-varying confounding.
ERA5 swvl1 is route-scale environmental context, not body hydration or pond depth.
No causal mediation or RC11 modification is authorized.
